_baseline_note: RE-RECORDED 2026-08-23 (215663 -> 224757, +4.2%) for the three-pass ISR and
the -O2 target build. The ceiling is a longest PATH through the call graph,
and it moved for two reasons that are both about SHAPE, not load: -O2 leaves
the 8-iteration tap loops rolled (so they are priced as loops with their full
trip count instead of as straight-line code the path can only partly take),
and the pitch/string/TIME paths are still all priced together because a
longest path cannot know they are mutually exclusive. The same edits cut the
hot-path TEXT from 13936 to 9174 bytes, which on a part that fetches from
5-wait-state flash is the direction that matters. See the tool's own header:
'restructuring the ISR can move it by tens of percent without the real load
moving at all'. The number that settles it is isr_pk on the unit.
_dl_cache_note: dl_cache's line fill (eng_frame loop 1) is the single most expensive burst
the model prices: 24 iterations of 4 SDRAM words, and a longest-PATH model is
free to assume every tap lane fills on the same frame. It cannot: dc_stencil
refuses a refill unless the lane's previous line survived DC_PAYBACK frames
(rule A) AND the token bucket has DC_FILL_COST tokens (rule B), which caps a
ALL eight lanes. The tool has no way to express a rate limit, and inventing
one would make it trust a claim instead of checking one, so the ceiling keeps
the pessimism. test/test_dl_cache.c and test/test_isr_budget.c check the real
bound; this file checks the shape of the code.
MEASURED (test_isr_budget, 2026-08-23): 3.06 SDRAM words per tap read in the
swept cases and exactly 4.00 (= the direct path) at the sustained varispeed
rail, against 4.00 direct. The pre-fix version measured 4.18 at the rail, i.e.
a net LOSS, and its fill compiled to a BYTE loop in one of the two inlined
copies of the tap loop (384 single-byte FMC reads per fill) — see dl_cache.h.
_readme: Manifest for tools/wcet.py — the machine-checkable half of budget
contract clause C-3. Every entry here is a CLAIM about the code that CI
re-checks on every build. `loops` is the number of cycles (strongly
connected components, reducible or not) the compiler emitted for that
function: it is deliberately brittle, because a change to it means the
loop structure of the audio ISR changed and a human must look. Bounds are
read out of each loop's own `cmp rN,#imm` exit test where one exists (see
infer_bound); `default_bound` covers the rest and needs the justification
in `why`. A loop with no edge leaving its body is rejected outright.
_sdram_note: These are the out-of-line readers of the external delay buffer; their
loads are priced at SDRAM_LOAD rather than SRAM. SDRAM traffic that the
compiler INLINED into bsp_audio_isr (dl_write, pt_read/pt_write, the
overdub read-modify-write) is still priced as SRAM — the model cannot
tell which pointer an inlined load followed. That underestimate is one of
the things the calibration ratio K absorbs; it is also why the ratio
between builds, not the absolute ceiling, is the regression signal.

_note: K = measured worst-case cycles / modelled ceiling, recorded with
--calibrate <isr_pk>. The ceiling assumes the most expensive branch
everywhere at once, so it is larger than any single real path; K says
by how much, for a build whose real load is known.
PROVENANCE of this value: the measurement is the lead's, isr_pk 4104 =
117% of budget in TIME/RECIRC with a loop playing, taken on the image
BEFORE workstream B's changes; the ceiling it is divided by is the
image AFTER them, because that is the one this tool can disassemble.
The two differ, so treat this K as an anchor of the right order and
re-record it next time the unit is on the bench: build, flash, reset
g_isr_pk, run the WCC-TIME programme, read isr_pk back, then
TWICE STALE AS OF THE A+B MERGE (2026-08-23): K was measured against an
image with neither workstream's engine changes, and is divided by a ceiling
that now carries the dl_cache pessimism above. The 158.1% it projects for
this build is therefore NOT a load estimate and must not be reported as one.
Re-record on the next bench session before quoting any projected percentage.

_index_note: Loops are indexed by wcet.py in (body-block-count, header-address) order, so
ANY codegen change can renumber them. Each `why` names the loop by what it
IS; the mapping was re-established from source by building with -g and
running arm-none-eabi-addr2line -i on every loop header address.
RE-ESTABLISHED 2026-08-23 for TWO changes at once: the ISR was split into
three passes (so engine_process_block is finally reached from the ISR rather
than only from the host tests), and the target image moved from -O3 to -O2
(see the Makefile: instruction fetch off 5-wait-state flash is a first-order
cost in a 14 KB ISR, and -O2 halves it). -O2 unrolls far less, so many of the
8-iteration tap loops that -O3 had flattened are real loops again — which is
why the counts went UP while the code got smaller. Do not renumber by eye.
Nearly every bound here is 8 = NUM_TAPS = DC_LANES = KS_STRINGS; the ones
that are not are the ones worth reading.

RE-ESTABLISHED 2026-09-30 for v1.3.1-rc1 (eng_frame 13 -> 14): the lookahead write limiter added its 8-entry running-max loop (new index 1); every other eng_frame loop kept its bound and only renumbered. Mapping re-done with FW_OPT='-O2 -g' (hex byte-identical) + addr2line -i on each header.

2026-09-30 (capture one-shot fix): splice_service 1 -> 2 loops (dc_invalidate_range, index 1 by header address). eng_frame unchanged in count; the splice bypass removal shortened the longest path (ceiling 218328 -> 183017).

0.why: ks.c:28, the Karplus-Strong string bank: KS_STRINGS = 8 rings per frame. Mutually exclusive with the pitch voice and with the tap reads (skip_tap_reads), but a longest-PATH model prices them all together — which is most of why the raw ceiling is ~4x budget.

1.why: main.c:688, the SWD dac-solo mask over the 8 TDM slots (bench scaffolding, g_dac_solo < 0 in normal use). TDM_SLOTS.

10.why: main.c PASS 2's per-frame branch — the pitch-voice and string-mode path, which keeps the old per-frame ordering because the voice reads the same SDRAM buffer between the engine's frames (issue #19). Same BLOCK_FRAMES bound; largest body in the image, which is the quickest way to re-identify it.

2.why: main.c:168, env_block_a()'s (1-a)^n power — computed once and cached, n = the runtime `frames` argument, clamped to BLOCK_FRAMES = 16 in the ISR prologue. This is the loop that makes the envelope pole track the block size the DMA actually hands over instead of the constant it was hard-coded for.

3.why: pitch_shift.c:581, grain-phase wrap `while (phase >= len) phase -= len`. The ratio is clamped to +/-2 octaves, so at most 4 whole grains can be crossed in one sample: 5 by construction.

4.why: pitch_shift.c:582, the negative-direction twin of loop 3.

5.why: main.c:623, the pitch-mode transposed-multitap read loop (each channel reads the voice's echo ring at its own tap delay). NUM_TAPS.

6.why: main.c PASS 1, the gather loop: codec word -> float, three |.| integrators, the input-rail test, the signal-in FM term. Bounded by `frames`, clamped to BLOCK_FRAMES = 16 in the prologue with a latched fault flag if the DMA ever disagrees.

7.why: engine_process_block's frame loop (engine.c:644), reached through the ISR's TIME-mode fast path — splice_service is inlined at its head. Same BLOCK_FRAMES bound. THIS LOOP IS THE POINT OF THE BRANCH: before the three-pass restructure the block API had no caller outside the host tests, so every per-block hoisting optimisation delivered exactly nothing on the unit.

8.why: main.c:686/689, the zero-fill of the TDM slots past NUM_TAPS. TDM_SLOTS = 8, so it is empty in the shipped configuration.

9.why: main.c:668, PASS 3's per-tap output stage: soft knee + 24-bit conversion, or a word copy on a frame the floor level held. NUM_TAPS.

0.why: dl_cache.h:215, dc_invalidate() inlined into dc_block_begin's disable path (the coherence kill switch). DC_LANES = 8.

1.why: dl_cache.h:245, the per-block lane ageing loop (lifetime rule 2 + the refill token bucket). DC_LANES = 8.

0.why: taps.c:77, taps_retarget's 8-lane Q32.32 target rebuild — runs whenever the control value moved, i.e. every sample while a knob or a CV is moving. NUM_TAPS.

1.why: engine.c:418, the overdub write limiter's LOOKAHEAD running max: the window max is max(partial, od_bmax[0..7]) — 8 sub-block maxima of OD_LOOKAHEAD/8 = 60 samples each, so every control value stays in the max for >= OD_LOOKAHEAD samples (v1.3.1-rc1, DAFx-02 Hämäläinen lookahead). Fixed 8, no data dependence. The matching 8-entry sub-block CLEAR at session end lives in od_session_end() and is unrolled by gcc at -O2; the 480-float ring is NOT cleared by a loop at all — a fill counter (od_ring_fill) makes it read as zero until refilled, precisely so that no 480-store burst exists on the ISR path (C-3a).

2.why: engine.c:486, the plain varispeed head advance `while (lp_phase >= 1) { advance; lp_phase -= 1; }`. lp_phase gains lp_rate per output sample and lp_rate is clamped to 4.0 in this same function: 4 whole samples plus a remainder = 5, by construction. If that clamp ever moves, this must move with it.

3.why: dl_cache.h:215, the per-FRAME dc_invalidate when the overdub loop or the splice job is writing where taps read (rule 3). DC_LANES.

4.why: engine.c:684, `declick_last[i] = taps[i]` — where the next transport fade starts from. NUM_TAPS.

5.why: mixer.c:25 via engine.c:599, mixer_channels() on the normal path.

6.why: engine.c:504, the chan[] zero-fill on the skip_tap_reads path (pitch and string modes own the outputs). NUM_TAPS.

7.why: engine.c:596, the floor level's hold: taps[i] = declick_last[i] instead of eight SDRAM reads. NUM_TAPS.

8.why: mixer.c:25 via engine.c:694, mixer_channels() on the HELD-frame path of the governor's floor level. NUM_TAPS.

9.why: engine.c:680, the transport declick crossfade over the 8 taps.

10.why: dl_cache.h:307, dc_stencil's line fill: `for (k = 0; k < DC_W; k += 4)`, DC_W = 96 floats four at a time = 24 iterations, and its loads are the most expensive in the image. MUST BE DECLARED: the exit test compares against a register, so infer_bound() returns None and it would fall back to default_bound = 8 — a 3x undercount of the largest FMC burst in the ISR. At -O2 gcc emits it as two LDRD + STRD/STR per iteration, i.e. genuine sequential word traffic (it emitted a BYTE loop here at -O3 before the may_alias rewrite — see dl_cache.h).

11.why: taps.c:87, taps_update's 8-lane one-pole slew in Q32.32.

12.why: engine.c:456, the OVERDUB write burst — the same varispeed while loop with the layered-input resample, the slew-gain write limiter and the FS clamp inside. Same 4.0 rate clamp, same bound of 5.

13.why: engine.c:604, THE 8-TAP READ LOOP: position, FM fold, window map, cache probe, interpolation. NUM_TAPS = 8. The governor's FLOOR level skips it entirely on alternate frames, which the ceiling does not model — this is the level-0 cost.

0.why: pitch_shift.c:76, the polyphase anti-alias convolution: AA_TAPS = 16 coefficients per output sample, morphed between band tables.

1.why: pitch_shift.c:68, the grain's 32-sample streaming cache refill — the redesign that replaced 32 uncached SDRAM loads per sample after the AA verify panel caught the naive version at ~2x the ISR idle budget. Fixed length, no data dependence.

0.why: engine.c:168, the seam-splice crossfade RMW loop. n = spl_quota * frames and both call sites pass frames = 1, with spl_quota capped at SPLICE_CHUNK = 8 in splice_arm (budget contract C-4). Stated explicitly rather than defaulted so that raising SPLICE_CHUNK is visible here. NOTE the derivation in splice_arm yields exactly 8 for every window the shipped constants allow — see engine.h.

1.why: dl_cache.h:223 via engine.c:208, dc_invalidate_range() after the splice RMW: 8 lanes, drop only the lines overlapping the samples just written (v1.3.1-rc2, bench session 9: the per-frame FULL invalidate while the splice ran = cache bypass for the whole splice window = 768 words/block = the one over-budget block at every loop capture). DC_LANES = 8, fixed, no data dependence.
